# Test fixtures

Every PDF here is **synthetic**, generated by `generate.mjs` with the raw writer in `pdf-writer.mjs`. No
customer artwork, no private documents, no third-party files. Nothing here needs a license beyond the
repository's own.

## Rules

- **Generated, never hand-edited.** Change a fixture by changing `generate.mjs`, then run
  `node tests/fixtures/generate.mjs`. The PDF and its `*.expected.json` are committed together.
- **Deterministic.** The writer emits no dates and a fixed file identifier, so a fresh build is byte-identical
  to the committed file. `node tests/fixtures/generate.mjs --check` (part of `npm test`) fails if they drift.
- **Expected values are stated, not measured.** Each fixture's expectations are written by hand in the
  generator, from the PDF specification, and never copied from the output of an engine under test.
  An engine is judged against them.
- **Asymmetric on purpose.** Box insets and marks differ on every edge, so a mirrored, rotated or swapped edge
  cannot pass by accident.
- **Raw dictionaries.** The writer writes page entries exactly as given, so invalid and inherited cases (boxes
  on the Pages node, inverted corners, illegal rotations) survive into the file.
- **Real documents stay out.** A real production PDF used to check a probe stays on the owner's machine and is
  never committed; findings from it are recorded in the plan without its content.

## Expected-value format

```json
{
  "fixture": "G1",
  "description": "…",
  "pages": [
    {
      "index": 0,
      "rotate": 0,
      "userUnit": 1,
      "boxes": {
        "TrimBox": { "raw": [19, 21, 576, 781], "effective": [19, 21, 576, 781], "origin": "explicit" }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

- `raw` is the array as written in the file, or `null` when the page has none.
- `effective` is the rectangle a correct reader uses, normalised to `[llx, lly, urx, ury]` in PDF user space.
- `origin` is `explicit`, `inherited`, `default` (a format fallback) or `invalid` (present but unusable).

## Mask fixtures (K1, K2a, K2m)

Mask pages are stated in **trim space**: every shape is a rectangle `[x, y, width, height]` in millimetres from
the TrimBox's lower-left corner, so registration is judged in the same terms whatever the page layout. K1 holds
artwork and masks in one PDF, out of order; K2a and K2m are an artwork PDF and a separate mask PDF whose pages
are opaque (trim placed elsewhere on a larger sheet), transparent, drawn 1.5 mm right and 1 mm down of their
nominal place, and 1 mm too wide. `samples` give the coverage expected at trim-relative points, at least 0.4 mm
from any edge.

## Model fixtures

`model/` holds project data as a project file may contain it, rather than PDFs. `mask-sources.json` lists stored
mask sources with the outcome each must have: supported kinds parse, future and unknown kinds are kept verbatim as
unsupported, and malformed entries are refused.
